ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.claim: The Abraham narrative, like the preceding anecdote, serves the same preaching purpose and also ends with the recurring verses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r7.anchor: the purpose of narrating this anecdote is the same as the one intended for the previous one.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.claim: The Abraham account fills the gap after Noah in the previous sūrah because Abraham was the most prominent messenger between Noah and Moses.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p418/r8.anchor: the most prominent messenger between Noah (sws) and Moses (sws) was Abraham (sws).

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r7.claim: Resurrection necessarily follows creation, sustenance, and guidance: recreating people is no harder than creating them, and this elaborate providence cannot end without consequence.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p422/r7.anchor: If creating it the first time was no cause of bother to God, how can re-creating it be of any bother.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.claim: Abraham presents the fundamentals of his preaching in logical order as personal impressions rather than argument, because in the acquittal and migration phase intellectual persuasion is useless; the subtle style may still stir hearts.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p423/r2.anchor: instead of presenting them through arguments and reasoning, he has expressed them in the form of personal impressions.

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r1.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r1.claim: Kashf al-Asrār says Abraham's illness was not known at the time but was a kind of feigning illness, like scholars who pretend to be sick to receive visitors.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r1.anchor: قال في "كشف الأسرار" : (وأين نه مرضى معلوم بود در آن وقت بلكه نوعي بود از تمارض) كما يتمارض الأحبار طمعا في العيادة

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r2.claim: The heart-healing alluded to here is Gabriel's occasional visit, commissioned by God to ask Abraham how he was; Abraham's inward answer rejoices that Gabriel asked.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r2.anchor: (آن شفاي ذدل خليل كه بوي أشارت ميكند آنست كه جبريل كاه كاه آمدي بفرمان حق وكفتي

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r3.claim: A sick, pale man who was urged to call a doctor replied that the doctor had made him ill, expressing reliance on God as the source of sickness.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r3.anchor: وحكي عن بعضهم أنه مرض وضعف اصفر لونه فقيل له ألا ندعو لك طبيبا

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r4.claim: God causes death at life's end and then raises people in the afterlife to repay their deeds; ثم marks the long interval between worldly death and resurrection.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r4.anchor: {والذى يميتنى} في الدنيا عند انقضاء الأجل {ثم يحيين} في الآخرة لمجازاة العمل أدخل ثم ههنا

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r5.claim: Death is attributed to God as a true divine favor because it can lead perfected people to eternal life and free them from trials and suffering.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r5.anchor: ونسبة الإماتة إلى الله تعالى لأنها من النعم الإلهية في الحقيقة حيث أن الموت وصلة لأهل الكمال إلى الحياة الأبدية والخلاص من أنواع المحن والبلية

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r6.speaker: الثعلبي
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī gives inward pairings: God kills by justice and revives by grace, or kills through sin, ignorance, greed, or separation and revives through obedience, intellect, piety, or union.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r6.anchor: أمام ثعلبي (كفته بميراند بعدل وزنده كند بفضل وكفته اندكه أماتت بمعصيت است واحيا بطاعت يا أماتت بجهل است واحيا بعقل

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r7.speaker: سلمى
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r7.claim: Salmi's Ḥaqāʾiq reading says God kills the self's ego and gives it life through divine guidance, which is true life.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r7.anchor: در حقايق سلمى آورده كه بميراند از سمات روحانيت وزنده كرداند بصفا تربانيت

BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r8.claim: A Persian couplet says one need not grieve when God is one's joy or fear when He is one's life, and need not attach the heart to the next world when God is one's present life.
BURSEVI:v6p206#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : غم كي خورد رنكه شادمانيش تويي باكي برد آنكه زندكانيش تويي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r7.claim: Death followed by resurrection needs no emphasis because only God can do it; Nimrod’s claim to give life and death is mere imposture and insolence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p165/r7.anchor: ولما كانت الإماتة بعد البعث، لا يمكن إسنادها إلا إلى الله، لم يحتج إلى توكيد ودعوى نمروذ الإماتة والإحياء هي منه على سبيل المخرفة والقحة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r3.claim: “Then” marks the temporal interval: God causes death in this world and gives life in the Hereafter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p118/r3.anchor: أدخل "ثم" هاهنا للتراخي، أي: يميتني في الدنيا ويحييني في الآخرة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:26:81-84/r1.claim: God causes death and then restores life in the hereafter.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r3.claim: God causes bodily death despite efforts to avert it and spiritual death through ignorance despite efforts to resist it; He revives physically with spirit and spiritually through guidance for the afterlife's recompense.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r3.anchor: أي حسا وإن اجتهدت في دفع الموت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r4.claim: The word ثم marks the greatness of resurrection and the long interval spent in the barzakh.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r4.anchor: أتى بأداة التراخي لذلك ولطول المكث في البرزخ

BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r5.claim: Abraham does not state exclusivity for giving life and death because only God had reported Nimrod's claim in al-Baqara; Abraham visibly demonstrated his inability to create a form, much less give or remove its spirit.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p368/r5.anchor: ولم يأت هنا بما يدل على الحصر لأنه لا مدعي للإحياء والإماتة إلا ما ذكره سبحانه عن نمروج في سورة البقرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r3.claim: The death clause is not restrictive because Ibrahim’s people did not assign death to idols; they attributed it to time or nature, or to God if they acknowledged divine creation and resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r3.anchor: فأما قوله : { والذي يميتني ثم يحيين } فلم يأت فيه بما يقتضي الحصر لأنهم لم يكونوا يزعمون أن الأصنام تميت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.claim: Repeating the relative pronoun rather than coordinating all clauses directly emphasizes the possessor of these three magnificent divine attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p143/r4.anchor: وتكرير اسم الموصول في المواضع الثلاثة مع أن مقتضى الظاهر أن تعطف الصلتان على الصلة الأولى للاهتمام بصاحب تلك الصلات الثلاث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.claim: The five divine acts span bodily and intellectual creation, food and water, illness and healing, death, and resurrection; together they trace physical life and the second life as gifts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r1.anchor: فذكر خلق الجسد وخلق العقل وإعطاء ما به بقاء المخلوق وهو الغذاء والماء ، وما يعتري المرء من اختلال المزاج وشفائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.claim: These descriptions also prepare for spiritual perfection: death looks like a blessing only after reflection, while the life after it is plainly a blessing for whoever wills it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r2.anchor: وذكر الموت الذي هو خاتمة الحياة الأولى ، وأعقبه بذكر الحياة الثانية للإشارة إلى أن الموت حالة لا يظهر كونها نعمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.claim: The first-person yāʾ is omitted from four verbs for lightness and rhyme at pauses, since most endings in this surah use a still nūn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v19p144/r3.anchor: وحذفت ياآت المتكلم من { يهدين ، ويسقين ، ويشفين ، ويحيين } لأجل التخفيف ورعاية الفاصلة لأنها يوقف عليها

JISHUMI:v7p5366/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5366/r18.claim: God's causing Abraham to die and then live means He postpones him until recompense.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r5.claim: Abraham presents death and resurrection as an inference, not a direct argument, since his audience disagreed about them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r5.anchor: وهذا قوله استدلالا ولم يقله احتجاجا , لأنهم خالفوه فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r6.claim: His point is that the favors his audience accepts entail the truth of what they dispute about death and resurrection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r6.anchor: فبين لهم أن ما وافقوه عليه موجب لما خالفوه فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.claim: The author rejects speculative interpretations that depart from the apparent meaning and what reason readily accepts.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r7.anchor: تجوز بعض المتعمقة في غوامض المعاني فعدل بذلك عن ظاهره إلى ما تدفعه بداهة العقول

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r11.claim: A speculative interpretation says God causes death through sins and life through acts of obedience.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r12.claim: Another interpretation says God causes death through fear and gives life through hope.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r13.claim: A further interpretation says God causes death through greed and life through contentment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r14.claim: The author says these interpretations are only ingenious embellishments and would have been better omitted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p175/r14.anchor: وهذه تأويلات تخرج عن حكم الاحتمال إلى جهة الاستطراف ، فلذلك ذكرناها وإن كان حذفها من كتابنا أولى

MUQATIL:26:69-85/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r11.claim: God causes Abraham to die in this world and then raises him after death in the next life.
MUQATIL:26:69-85/r11.anchor: بعد الموت فى الآخرة، { والذي أطمع } يعنى أرجو { أن يغفر لي خطيئتي يوم الدين } [آية: 82] يعنى يوم الحساب،

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r5.claim: Resurrection is intended; although people ascribed death to causes, God alone causes death and gives life.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r5.anchor: وكانوا ينسبون الموت إلى الأسباب فبين أن الله هو الذي يميت ويحيي.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r12.speaker: أهل الإشارات
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r12.claim: Six allegories pair death through sin, fear, or greed with life through obedience, hope, or contentment.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r12.anchor: فالذي يميتني بالمعاصي يحييني بالطاعات. الثاني: يميتني بالخوف يحييني بالرجاء. الثالث: يميتني بالطمع ويحييني بالقناعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r13.speaker: أهل الإشارات
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r13.claim: Further allegories pair death through justice, separation, or ignorance with life through grace, reunion, or reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r13.anchor: قول رابع: يميتني بالعدل ويحييني بالفضل. وقول خامس: يميتني بالفراق ويحييني بالتلاق. وقول سادس: يميتني بالجهل ويحييني بالعقل

QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r14.claim: Qurtubi rejects these obscure allegories as the verse's intent: inward symbols cannot be meant for people ignorant of truth while plain meanings are abandoned.
QURTUBI-FULL:26:78-81/r14.anchor: إلى غير ذلك مما ليس يشيء منه مراد من الآية فإن هذه التأويلات الغامضة، والأمور الباطنة، إنما تكون لمن حذق وعرف الحق،

RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r14.claim: Dying means release from worldly afflictions and punishments, and being brought back to life means receiving recompense.
RAZI-FULL:v24p124#3/r14.anchor: الإماتة في الدنيا والتخلص عن آفاتها وعقوباتها

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.claim: Only a being capable of the listed acts is worthy of worship.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r1.anchor: Only a being capable of the acts listed in these verses is worthy and deserving of worship

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.claim: Symbolically, God nourishes the soul, heals its ailments, and enlivens the spirit by bringing death to the passionate ego.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r2.anchor: Interpreted symbolically, these verses can mean that God feeds and nourishes the soul, heals the ailments of the soul, and enlivens the spirit

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.speaker: Al-Thaʿlabī
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī describes spiritual death and life as justice and grace, disobedience and obedience, separation and meeting God, and ignorance and knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r5.anchor: Al-Thaʿlabī summarizes the spiritual dimensions of these verses by saying that God brings death through justice and life through grace

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.speaker: Su
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.claim: Others say people die outwardly yet live inwardly, die through forgetting God, and live through remembering Him.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r6.anchor: one is caused to die outwardly, but is given life inwardly, dies through forgetfulness of God, and lives through remembrance of Him (Su)

STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.speaker: Junayd
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.claim: Junayd compares resurrection to nakedness, hunger, and thirst, except for those clothed in reverence and given gnosis and love.
STUDYQURAN:26:78/r7.anchor: Some quote Junayd, who says that when human beings are resurrected on the Day of Judgment

SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq, also reportedly followed by ʿĀṣim, retains the first-person yāʾ in yasqīn, yashfīn, and yuḥyīn.
SAMIN-DURR:26:79/r3.anchor: وأثبت ابن أبي إسحاق وتروى عن عاصم أيضا ياء المتكلم في " يسقين " و " يشفين " و " يحيين ".

TABATABAI:26:79-81/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r6.claim: Death is the decreed death every soul tastes, not annihilation but transition between abodes within universal governance; resurrection is the bestowal of life after death.
TABATABAI:26:79-81/r6.anchor: كل نفس ذائقة الموت الأنبياء 35، وليس بانعدام وفناء بل انتقال من دار إلى دار

TABRISI:26:78-84/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r7.claim: God causes Abraham's death after life and will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection after death.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r7.anchor: أي يميتني بعد أن كنت حيا ويحييني يوم القيامة بعد أن أكون ميتا.

TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.claim: The final yāʾ letters are omitted because these are verse endings.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r11.anchor: وإنما حذف الياءات لأنه رؤوس الآيات

TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.claim: Abraham's speech argues against his people that only the one who performs these acts deserves divinity.
TABRISI:26:78-84/r12.anchor: وهذا الكلام من إبراهيم ع إنما صدر على وجه الاحتجاج على قومه والإخبار بأنه لا يصلح للإلهية إلا من فعل هذه الأفعال.

THALABI:v7p169/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p169/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p169/r5.claim: The word “then” in “He causes me to die, then revives me” marks separation and delay.
THALABI:v7p169/r5.anchor: والذي يميتني ثم يحيين أدخل هاهنا (ثم) للقطع والتراخي

THALABI:v7p169/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p169/r6.speaker: أهل اللسان والإشارة
THALABI:v7p169/r6.claim: The people of language and allusion give spiritual contrasts: God causes death through justice, sin, separation, abandonment, richness, and ignorance, and life through grace, obedience, reunion, success, that same richness, and knowledge.
THALABI:v7p169/r6.anchor: قال أهل اللسان والإشارة: يميتني بالعدل ويحييني بالفضل، يميتني بالمعصية ويحييني بالطاعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70#2/r1.claim: Maqatil glosses the expression “and the one who causes me to die” with “I hope,” completing the sense of Abraham's hope in the following clause.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p507#2/r6.claim: “The one who causes me to die and then gives me life” refers to resurrection.

QIRAAT-ER:26:81:5#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:26:81:5#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:26:81:5#1/r1.claim: The form with explicit suffix yāʾ contrasts with Ḥafṣ's deleted yāʾ; the difference is orthographic and does not affect meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:26:81:5#1/r1.anchor: Yz, mutawatir: Full spelling of the 1st person object suffix with explicit yāʾ — yuḥyīnī vs Ḥafṣ yuḥyīni

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r1.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r1.claim: Ibn al-Munir explains that death is a universally known, inevitable decree, so sharing it lessens its sting and permits attributing it to God; illness is a particular affliction, so good manners attribute it to oneself and its proximate cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r1.anchor: الموت قد علم واشتهر أنه قضاء محتوم من الله عز وجل على سائر البشر وحكم عام لايخص

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r4.claim: Al-Alusi faults al-Zamakhshari for overlooking the distinction above: illness-related death can also follow human negligence, yet Ibrahim attributes death generally to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r4.anchor: غفل عن أن المعنى الذي ابدأه في المرض ينكسر بالموت أيضا فان المرض كما يكون بسبب تفريط الانسان

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r5.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r5.claim: Some eminent scholars say death and revival are paired because they are among God's defining prerogatives and underpin the affairs of the afterlife; death is a passage to eternal life, not something to recoil from.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r5.anchor: حيث كانت معظم خصائصه عز وجل كالاحياء بدءا وإعادة وقد نيطت أمور الآخرة جميعا بها وبما بعدها من البعث

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r6.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the further explanation that, for the perfected, death leads to eternal good they value above worldly life and frees sinners from further sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r6.anchor: وأولى من هذه العلاوة ما قيل : إن الموت لأهل الكمال وصلة نيل المحاب الأبدية

ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r8.claim: ثم marks temporal delay because the intended revival is resurrection, which follows death in time even though every future event is near.
ALUSI-FULL:v19p96#3/r8.anchor: و ( ثم ) في قوله ( ثم يحيين ) للتراخي الزماني

DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet promises guidance, Paradise food and drink, healing and expiation, blessed life and martyrdom, forgiveness, wisdom, truthful renown, and Paradise homes for one who recites Abraham’s prayer after ablution while leaving for obligatory prayer; al-Ḥasan adds a prayer for the parents.
DURR-FULL:v6p306/r4.anchor: عن سمرة بن جندب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا توضأ العبد لصلاة مكتوبة فاسبغ الوضوء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r1.claim: The people did not deny death but attributed its cause to something other than God's decree; Abraham attributes it to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r1.anchor: أن القوم كانوا لا ينكرون الموت وإنما يجعلون له سببا سوى تقدير الله عز وجل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r2.claim: Abraham means resurrection, which the people denied; he argues that what they accept about death entails the truth of what they reject about resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p129#4/r2.anchor: وقوله ثم يحيين يعني البعث وهو امر لا يقرون به وإنما قاله استدلالا عليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147/r1.claim: God alone gives life and death; no one else can do so, for He originates creation and brings it back.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p147/r1.anchor: هو الذي يحيي ويميت، لا يقدر على ذلك أحد سواه، فإنه هو الذي يبدئ ويعيد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r1.claim: Abraham says God causes him to die rather than when I die because death is passage from affliction and perishing to abiding life in hope of meeting God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r1.anchor: ولم يقل إذا مت لأنه الخروج من حبس البلاء ودار الفناء إلى روض البقاء لوعد اللقاء

NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r2.claim: Thumma marks the interval between death and resurrection; fa is used for guidance and healing because they follow creation and illness directly.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p189#2/r2.anchor: وأدخل ثم فى الإحياء لتراخيه عن الافناء وادخل الفاء في الهداية والشفاء لأنهما يعقبان الخلق والمرض

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r1.claim: God causes me to die through fear of Him and revives me through hope in Him.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : الذي يميتني بخوفه ، ويحييني برجائه

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r2.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r2.claim: He causes me to die away from Him, then revives me through Him.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : الذي يميتني عنه ثم يحييني به

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r3.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r3.claim: For the community, He causes me to die to myself and gives me life through Him.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r3.anchor: قال ذو النون رحمه الله : وعلى الجماعة في هذه الآية الذي يميتني عن نفسي

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r4.claim: He causes me to die through veiling and revives me through manifestation.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r4.anchor: قال الواسطي ورحمه الله : الذي يميتني بالاستتار ويحييني بالتجلي

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r5.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r5.claim: He causes me to die through heedlessness and revives me through remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r5.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : الذي يميتني بالغفلة ثم يحييني بالذكر

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r6.speaker: ذو النون
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r6.claim: He kills my heart to this world and revives it through nearness to Him.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r6.anchor: ذو النون رحمه الله : يميت قلبي

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r7.claim: He causes me to die through sins and revives me through acts of obedience.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الذي يميتني بالمعاصي ويحييني بالطاعات

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r8.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r8.claim: He causes me to die through need of Him and revives me through independence from Him.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r8.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمه الله : الذي يميتني بالافتقار إليه ويحييني بالاستغناء عنه

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r9.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r9.claim: He causes me to die through heedlessness and revives me through remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r9.anchor: وقال سهل رحمه الله : الذي يميتني بالغفلة ، ويحييني بالذكر

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r10.speaker: الخراز
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r10.claim: He makes me independent of myself and keeps me alive through Himself.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r10.anchor: وقال الخراز : الذي يغنيني عني ، ويبقيني به

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r11.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r11.claim: He causes me to die through trials and revives me through blessings.

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r12.speaker: محمد بن حامد
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r12.claim: He causes me to die through greed and revives me through contentment.
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r12.anchor: محمد بن حامد : الذي يميتني بالطمع

SULAMI:v2p76#3/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r13.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p76#3/r13.claim: He causes me to die outwardly and revives me inwardly.

TUSTARI:26:81/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:26:81/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:26:81/r1.claim: God causes the speaker to die through heedlessness and revives him through remembrance.
TUSTARI:26:81/r1.anchor: الذي يميتني بالغفلة ثم يحييني بالذكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and commentators understand God as causing death in this world and raising the dead for resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r1.anchor: في الدنيا {ثم يحيين} للبعث. قاله ابن عباس، والمفسرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r2.claim: The compositional analyst says they accepted death but assigned it a cause other than God and denied resurrection; Abraham declares God causes both death and life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r2.anchor: كانوا لا يدفعون الموت، إلا أنهم يجعلون له سببا سوى الله، ويكفرون بالبعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r3.claim: ثم marks the interval between death and life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p70/r3.anchor: ودخلت (ثم) للتراخي الذي بين الموت والحياة

BURHAN:v4p68/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p68/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p68/r6.claim: Then marks the interval between death and resurrection; the people did not deny that God causes death, but denied resurrection.
BURHAN:v4p68/r6.anchor: ولم يكونوا منكرين الموت من الله وإنما انكروا البعث فدخلت ثم لتراخي ما بين الاماتة والاحياء

ITQAN:v3p293/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.claim: Al-Tibi says Abraham’s speech combines a graceful transition and a good request: he moves from God’s attributes to “My Lord, grant me judgment and join me with the righteous.”
ITQAN:v3p293/r3.anchor: قال الطيبي ومما اجتمع فيه حسن التخلص والمطلب معا قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم

ITQAN:v3p240/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.claim: Al-Tafwit is presenting varied meanings, such as praise and description, in separate sentences of equal measure; it may use long, medium, or short sentences.
ITQAN:v3p240/r1.anchor: هو إتيان المتكلم بمعان شتى من المدح والوصف وغير ذلك من الفنون كل فن في جملة منفصلة

ITQAN:v3p240/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.claim: Abraham's successive statements about God's guidance, provision, healing, death, and revival exemplify al-tafwit in long sentences.
ITQAN:v3p240/r2.anchor: فمن الطويلة ﴿ الذي خلقني فهو يهدين والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.claim: In Abraham's account, fa links creation to guidance without delay, while thumma marks resurrection as delayed after death.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f11.anchor: فقد عطف في الآية الأولى بالفاء لتعقب بلا مهلة الهداية للخلق

NASHR:v2p336/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p336/r10.speaker: يعقوب
NASHR:v2p336/r10.claim: Yaqub affirms the sixteen listed extra yāʾs in both connected and pause forms: the eight quoted forms plus أطيعون in eight places.
NASHR:v2p336/r10.anchor: أثبت الياء في جميعها يعقوب في الحالين
